name: Commodity value (5-year price reversal)

origin.source_title: Value and Momentum Everywhere (Journal of Finance 68(3), 2013)

how_it_works.simple: Buy the commodities whose prices have fallen most over the past five years and sell those that rose most, betting that extremes partly undo themselves.
how_it_works.analogy: Like buying winter coats in summer: what is out of favour for long enough tends to come back.
how_it_works.precise: Value signal: minus the log change in spot price over five years (average price 4.5 to 5.5 years ago over today). AQR's century study reports a Sharpe ratio of 0.38 for commodity value over 1926 to 2020, 0.50 in the original sample and 0.44 after publication.

rule: Monthly: rank energy contracts by -ln(P_t / average price 54 to 66 months ago); long the cheapest, short the dearest, inverse volatility weights.
economic_rationale: Supply responds slowly to prices: high prices bring new supply and low prices close mines and wells, so extremes partly revert over several years.
why_it_might_fail: Four energy contracts give a thin cross-section; the signal needs five years of history; commodity value has long dry spells.

reported_results.source: Ilmanen, Israel, Lee, Moskowitz and Thapar (2021), JOIM, Table 1
reported_results.notes: Table 2: Sharpe 0.22 before, 0.50 during and 0.44 after the original sample. AQR's own backtest.

post_publication_evidence: AQR's post-publication Sharpe ratio of 0.44 (Ilmanen et al., 2021).

relevance.reason: Supported after publication; most useful as part of a combined carry, value and momentum commodity strategy.
